While versions of Q-Res (without the NP oracle) underly proof systems for QCDCL [15], the connection between QNP – Res and CAQECORE appears nontrivial. This is why we will make use of decision lists, which represent strategies and even characterise QNP – Res on bounded quantifier alternation [4].

context: We would like to comment that it is unclear whether @Red ` Res simulates the non-oracle version of CAQECORE , or even the general algorithmic CAQE paradigm. While the Res refutations π in @Red ` Res proofs somehow correspond to the refutations ρ generated by a SAT solver during a CAQECORE run, there might not be a polynomial-time transformation between those two. The reason is that the latter uses the auxiliary B-variables from CAQECORE , while the former does not. Resolving over those B-variables first would effectively eliminate them, but this might result in an exponential blow-up in the proof size. On the other hand, redefining @Red ` Res by allowing B-variables in the refutations π could cause other problems: In [35] it was proven that @Red ` Res is equivalent to level-ordered Q-Res. For the first direction, one can argue that all π simply have to be stuck together in order to obtain a level-ordered Q-Res refutation. Allowing B-variables in π could render this simulation impossible. We avoid these potential issues by adding an NP oracle and disregarding Res refutations both for @Red ` Res as well as for CAQECORE . If the simulation of CAQECORE by @Red ` Res indeed holds without NP oracles, then the result in Theorem 8 would follow trivially (as well as the simulation of CAQECORE by QNP – Res). But whether or not this holds remains open. 5 Strategy extraction and soundness/completeness of CAQE In this section we will show how to perform strategy extraction on CAQECORE proofs. Strategy extraction is a common technique not only for obtaining lower bounds, but also for proving the soundness of a proof system. More precisely, from a given CAQECORE refutation we extract a universal winning strategy, whereas from a CAQECORE verification we extract an existential winning strategy. This results in strategy size as a lower bound for the size of CAQECORE proofs. From now on, if not otherwise specified, we will always assume that Φ is a QCNF with prefix @U0 DX1 @U1 DX2 @U2 . . .
